sides.name: Grand Alliance (Marlborough, Eugene)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. 52,000 and 66 guns. Infantry/cavalry split derived from nominal battalion (~500) and squadron (~120) strengths, educated guess. Weapons 5.6: flintlock, socket bayonet, British platoon fire. Logistics 5.8: the march to the Danube with pre-arranged magazines. Command 0.95: Marlborough and Eugene.

sides.name: France and Bavaria (Tallard, Marsin, Maximilian II Emanuel)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. 56,000 and 90 guns. Split derived as for the Allies. Villages of Blenheim and Oberglauheim barricaded and packed with infantry (field works, not a fortified city). Command 0.4: three uncoordinated commanders; 27 battalions trapped in Blenheim village surrendered.

outcome.note: Allied victory. Allies 4,542 killed, 7,942 wounded, 500 captured. Franco-Bavarians 6,000 killed or drowned, 7,000 wounded, 14,190 captured (27,190); higher totals in the literature include stragglers and deserters, mid 30,000 placed between. Main attacks from about 13:00, Blenheim garrison surrendered about 21:00.
